REVISE

- **blocker** `packages/core/src/modules/staff/data/validators.ts:148` — An extension composes either exported job-history schema with Zod .partial() or .extend(); Zod throws at runtime on a refined schema, breaking existing schema consumers covered by BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md; Keep the existing exported objects composable and apply date-range validation through internal write-only schemas or a shared command guard.
- **minor** `packages/core/src/modules/staff/data/validators.ts:132` — A create or update supplies both dates in the wrong order while the request uses a non-English locale; The schema returns English on endDate, while one-field updates return translated feedback for the same problem; Translate the same field error at the API boundary for both schema and merged-date failures and cover the locale behavior.

- `changes-requested` — The review found changes needed before approval.
- `needs-qa` — The change affects saving from the staff job history form.
- `priority-medium` — This is a routine staff data validation fix.
- `risk-high` — The diff changes how downstream callers can compose exported validator schemas.
🤖 `om-auto-review-pr` — handoff to @pcbeingused333. Please address the findings in the [code review](https://github.com/open-mercato/open-mercato/pull/10568#pullrequestreview-6047408265).

Thanks @haxiorz, good catch. The exported create/update Zod schemas are plain objects again (no refinements), so `.partial()`/`.extend()` work as before. The date-range check now lives in a shared guard in the job history commands: it runs on create and on update (merged stored + patched dates) and returns a translated `fieldErrors.endDate`. I added a test that the exported schema is still extendable. PR description updated.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
